audit.title: Subscription Method (VRF v2.5)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections generally lead with the answer — "Each subscription supports up to 100 consuming contracts" is exemplary and liftable. The page-level opener ("This section explains how to…") is meta rather than a self-contained definition; weak but minor.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy (11 headings, 1 H1, H4 max depth, 0 level skips per measured facts). But 0 tables — the limits and gas-variable content is list-only where a comparison table would extract better; one section exceeds 600 words.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong specifics — 24-hour expiry, 10/5/3 LINK worked example, 200,000 gwei, 100-consumer cap, 50-value example. Vague quantifiers ("several", "quickly") appear but are peripheral.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 3 GitHub primary-source links to the actual coordinator/base contracts is good. Weakness: 3 links use opaque anchor text ("here") that engines can't attribute — "found [here]" appears three times for supported-networks.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Bolded concept list ("**Subscription id:** 256-bit unsigned integer…") is verbatim-liftable and well-formed. Strong.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. No freshness or entity signals for engines to trust or parse. Head metadata could not be verified — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Single solidity block shows only the `requestRandomWords` call with no imports, no contract wrapper, no `VRFV2PlusClient` import path. Not copy-paste runnable on its own.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup → request → limits lifecycle well, but no FAQ/troubleshooting and no error/symptom phrasing. Debug-path queries are unserved by heading structure.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Consistent product naming (VRF v2.5, VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus, coordinator) and unambiguous prose. Strong; no action needed.

audit.summary: This page cleanly explains the VRF v2.5 subscription funding model — core concepts, the request/receive lifecycle, and subscription/coordinator limits — with well-bolded definitions and useful hard numbers (256-bit subscription IDs, 100-consumer cap, 24-hour pending expiry, 200,000 gwei max verification gas). Its biggest GEO strength is clear, chunkable definitional prose; its biggest opportunity is retrieval-side: there is no structured metadata (0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, no dates) and no symptom-phrased troubleshooting coverage, so error-driven queries ("my VRF request is stuck pending", "callback fails but subscription charged") won't retrieve this page even though it answers them. The single solidity snippet is also incomplete (no imports, no contract scaffold), limiting agent-runnability.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: Debug facts are buried in prose; "requests remain pending for up to 24 hours before they expire."
recommendations.change: Add H3s phrased as queries: "Why is my VRF request stuck pending?" (answer: balance below minimum → pending up to 24h, auto-processes after top-up) and "Why was my subscription charged when the callback failed?" (answer: insufficient `callbackGasLimit` → callback fails but subscription still charged for randomness generation).
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom and error, not concept; the answers already exist verbatim but no heading matches the query.

recommendations.title: Add a limits summary table
recommendations.issue: 0 tables; caps are scattered across prose and lists.
recommendations.change: One table with columns Limit / Value / Notes — rows for Max consumers (100), Minimum balance (Max Cost buffer), Max verification gas (200,000 gwei), `MAX_NUM_WORDS` (per-network), `maxGasLimit` (per-network), pending expiry (24 hours).
recommendations.why: Tables are high-lift for extraction and let engines build justified, numeric answers.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical, and last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured facts: 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink VRF v2.5"`, canonical URL, and `programmingLanguage: Solidity`; surface a visible "Last updated" date.
recommendations.why: Freshness and entity signals raise trust and parseability; site-level fix but page-scoped here.

recommendations.title: Complete the solidity snippet
recommendations.where: the `requestRandomWords` block under "Set up your contract and request"
recommendations.issue: Snippet shows the call only; measured facts confirm the block shows no imports.
recommendations.change: Wrap in a minimal contract inheriting `VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus`, with the `import` for `VRFV2PlusClient`, the `s_vrfCoordinator` declaration, and a stub `fulfillRandomWords`. Tag the fence `solidity` and note pragma `^0.8`.
recommendations.why: Agents copy runnable snippets; a bare call forces cross-page assembly and invites parametric-prior guesses at imports.

recommendations.title: Replace opaque link anchors
recommendations.change: Rewrite as "see the [VRF v2.5 supported networks](/vrf/v2-5/supported-networks) page."
recommendations.why: Descriptive anchor text is attributable and improves link-based retrieval signals.

recommendations.title: Lead the page with a canonical one-sentence definition
recommendations.where: opening line "This section explains how to generate random numbers…"
recommendations.issue: Meta framing, not a liftable definition.
recommendations.change: Open with: "A VRF v2.5 subscription is a prepaid account that funds randomness requests from multiple consuming contracts in LINK or native tokens, reducing per-request gas cost."
recommendations.why: A self-contained first sentence resists parametric priors and is directly quotable.

recommendations.title: Name the EOA anti-pattern as an explicit Don't
recommendations.issue: "do **not** attempt to use EOAs to send VRF requests directly" is present but embedded in prose.
recommendations.change: Break out as a bolded "Don't:" callout with the correct pattern first: "Requests must originate from your consuming contract, not directly from an EOA."
recommendations.why: Explicit Don'ts with the canonical pattern first defend against the common-but-wrong shortcut when the page is skimmed.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers "several" and "quickly" where a number would serve.
One section exceeds 600 words (chunk-boundary risk for RAG).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already linked at the top — good; ensure it lists this URL with a descriptive summary.
JSON-LD/canonical/date emission is likely a site-template concern; fixing it benefits the whole `docs.chain.link` corpus, not just this page.
The CLI captured no `<head>` — pass raw head HTML next run to verify metadata rather than infer absence.
